title: Eval-Driven Pinning Policy and Intake Acceptance Checklist for Open Model Submissions
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: define a deterministic, eval-driven policy and lightweight acceptance checklist for ingesting new open models into the Redwood model catalog. This ticket captures the PRD-level requirements, scope boundaries, and concrete acceptance criteria that will be used by intake reviewers (PM/Eng/Research) to decide: accept (pinned or soft-pinned), accept-with-conditions, or reject. Motivation: we are seeing an increase in community-submitted weights with varied runtime characteristics and undocumented op dependencies. Without clearer intake rules we risk runtime incompatibility regressions, unpredictable latency/cost changes for customers, and catalog churn. This document prioritizes: 1) a measurable gating surface (eval signals + runtime sanity checks) 2) minimal friction for high-quality community models 3) clear guidance for pinning and fallback behavior.
scope_included: New open model submissions (community weights, permissive license)
Automated runtime sanity test definitions (baseline, P95 latency, memory),
Eval rubric and delta thresholds vs curated baseline models
Catalog metadata and compatibility notes required for intake
scope_excluded: Detailed hardware procurement or scheduling changes
Full security audit of model provenance (handled by separate legal/compliance flow)
requirements: Intake form must require: model_name, release_tag, model_hash (SHA256), tokenizer_type, max_context_tokens, expected_embedding_dim (if applicable), declared ops list (top-level custom kernels)
Automated quick-run on a small standardized eval set (50 prompts) measuring P95 latency, token throughput, mem-peak on reference infra (A100/32GB equivalent)
Quality eval: 1k prompt eval comparing to selected baseline on relevance/factuality with a pass threshold of <= 5% regression in primary metric
Compatibility metadata: declared quantization compatibility (yes/no), expected KV-cache shape, tokenizer vocabulary file link
Runtime sanity: failure modes (OOM, unsupported op, fatal kernel error) must be low-confidence flags and surface human-readable diagnostics in intake UI
Pinning decision matrix: automatically suggest pin level (unpinned / soft-pin / hard-pin) based on eval + runtime signals
acceptance_criteria: Intake UI enforces required metadata fields and blocks submissions without model_hash and tokenizer_type
Automatic eval job runs for a submitted model and produces a report within 2 hours for models <10B parameters
A model is marked soft-pin when runtime signals indicate compatibility but eval shows small regression (<= 5%) AND no unsupported ops detected
A model is marked hard-pin when the model requires a specific runtime variant or kernel set to function and there is no compatible fallback
Reject if automated runtime sanity tests fail with fatal errors (unsupported kernel) or if eval regression exceeds 15% on primary metric
Intake report includes clear recommended rollout policy: canary % default, fallback model id, and suggested quantization profile if applicable
Acceptance requires signoff by PM + an Engineer's acknowledgement of runtime compatibility (checkbox)
eval_signals_and_thresholds: Primary quality delta threshold (vs baseline): <=5% = acceptable, 5-15% = conditional, >15% = reject
Latency budget: P95 must not exceed baseline by more than 30% for interactive-tier catalog entries
Memory overhead: peak GPU memory <= 1.3x baseline or flagged for dedicated-only placement
Unsupported op ratio: any unknown op triggers engineer review; >0.5% unknown op prevalence on calls -> reject
Tokenization mismatch: tokenizer must map to expected embedding dim or fail intake
pinning_policy_and_decisions: Default behavior: prefer soft-pin with automatic routing to a verified runtime variant when quality is within threshold and runtime compatible
Hard-pin reserved for cases where the model requires a non-standard kernel, unique quantization path, or architecture-level divergence (eg. custom attention) that blocks fallback
Soft-pin semantics: allow traffic to shift to unpinned runtime variants over time once compatibility tests and real traffic signals are good, with a configurable decay window (default 14 days)
Pin exemptions: toy/test weights or models under active research can be marked 'no-pin' by PM with a short TTL and explicit consumer warning
ui_and_catalog_requirements: Intake flow must show eval summary, runtime sanity results, and suggested pin level before final submission
Catalog entry must surface 'compatibility_notes' text field of at least 200 chars explaining any known runtime caveats
Model pages should show per-hardware P95 latency and recommended quantization settings
Reviewer dashboard: filterable list of pending intakes sorted by risk score (eval delta + unknown-op count + memory delta)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement intake metadata enforcement and automated quick-run eval jobs
Phase 2 (2 weeks): integrate runtime sanity checks and pinning suggestion engine in reviewer dashboard
Phase 3 (1 week): design review for catalog UI text and compatibility_notes guidance; beta with internal teams
Phase 4: public rollout with an authoring checklist and short docs for community contributors
tradeoffs_and_decisions_notes: Tradeoff: tight thresholds reduce risk but increase intake friction for community models; we choose soft-pin as default to balance risk vs friction
Decision: require model_hash and tokenizer_type to reduce provenance ambiguity
Decision: engine signoff remains manual for unknown-op cases to avoid silent failures in production
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: automated evals may produce false negatives on niche promptsets - mitigation: require PM review for conditional passes
Risk: unknown op proliferation that blocks intake - mitigation: expand our kernel compatibility matrix and add signal to flag op authorships
Risk: increased reviewer load - mitigation: risk score and automation suggestions to triage low-risk accepts
